spawn_spec.prompt:
TASK: Build the browser playback runtime that animates a LibreOffice-rendered slide SVG from a PowerPoint-derived timeline. This is an executable coding assignment, not a research handoff.

REPO: C:\Users\steve\Desktop\projects\impromptu-r2 — a Bun 1.3 monorepo (workspaces: apps/*, services/*, packages/*), TypeScript 5.9 strict, Biome, tests with `bun test`.

DELIVERABLE (a NEW workspace package you fully own — do not modify existing packages):
packages/slide-runtime/
  package.json          (name "@impromptu/slide-runtime", private, type module, exports ./src/index.ts, scripts: typecheck via `tsc --noEmit`, test via `bun test`)
  tsconfig.json         (mirror packages/contracts/tsconfig.json — read it and match strictness exactly)
  src/index.ts          (named exports only)
  src/timeline.ts       (Zod schemas parsing the timeline JSON produced by the Python renderer)
  src/player.ts         (the Web Animations API player)
  src/timeline.test.ts
  src/player.test.ts

THE TIMELINE CONTRACT (already frozen in Python at services/ingestion/src/impromptu_ingestion/render/contracts.py — READ IT FIRST and mirror it exactly in Zod; field names are snake_case on the wire):
- SlideTimeline: { slide_key: string, click_groups: SlideEffect[][], transition?: { kind: string, advance_on_click: boolean } | null, unsupported: { reason_code: string, preset_id?: number|null, detail: string }[] }
- SlideEffect: { trigger: "on_click"|"with_previous"|"after_previous", effect_class: "entrance"|"emphasis"|"exit"|"motion", preset_id: number, preset_subtype?: number|null, duration_ms: number, delay_ms: number, target: { shape_id: number, shape_name: string, svg_element_id: string }, behavior: Behavior }
- Behavior is a discriminated union on `kind`: { kind: "fade", direction: "in"|"out" } | { kind: "wipe", direction: "in"|"out", edge: "left"|"right"|"up"|"down" } | { kind: "motion", path: string } | { kind: "color", from_color: string, to_color: string }

WHAT TO BUILD:
A. timeline.ts — Zod schemas + `parseSlideTimeline(input: unknown): SlideTimeline` that rejects anything malformed (parse, don't validate). Export inferred types. The union must be a real discriminated union (z.discriminatedUnion on "kind").
B. player.ts — `createSlidePlayer(options: { svgRoot: SVGSVGElement; timeline: SlideTimeline }): SlidePlayer` where SlidePlayer exposes:
   - `readonly groupCount: number`
   - `readonly currentGroup: number` (0 = nothing played yet)
   - `advance(): Promise<void>` — plays the next click group: ON_CLICK effect starts the group, WITH_PREVIOUS effects start simultaneously with the effect before them, AFTER_PREVIOUS effects start when the previous one finishes. Resolves when the group's animations finish.
   - `reset(): void` — returns every targeted element to its pre-animation state.
   - `readonly state: "ready" | "playing" | "finished"`
   Implementation rules:
   - Resolve each effect's element with `svgRoot.getElementById(effect.target.svg_element_id)`; a missing element is a typed error (a SlideRuntimeError subclass carrying a machine-readable `code`), never a silent skip.
   - ENTRANCE effects must set the element hidden (opacity 0 / visibility) BEFORE the show starts — call an explicit `prepare()` at construction that hides every element targeted by an entrance effect in a later click group, so the initial frame is correct. This is essential: an entrance animation whose element is already visible is a wrong render.
   - Drive animations with `element.animate(keyframes, { duration, delay, fill: "forwards", easing })` (Web Animations API). fade -> opacity; color -> the `fill` presentation attribute (SVG shapes are filled via `fill`, not CSS `color`); wipe -> a clip-path inset animation from the named edge; motion -> a `transform: translate()` animation derived from the OOXML relative path.
   - MOTION PATH DETAIL: OOXML motion paths use coordinates that are FRACTIONS OF THE SLIDE (e.g. "M 0 1 L 0 0 E" means start one slide-height below and travel to the origin), commands are M/L/C/Z with a trailing "E" marker meaning end-of-path. Convert to pixel offsets using the SVG viewBox dimensions, emit a transform keyframe list, and treat any command you cannot convert exactly as a typed error rather than an approximation.
   - Unsupported effects: if `timeline.unsupported.length > 0`, `createSlidePlayer` must THROW a typed error (code "deck_not_animatable") unless the caller passes `{ allowUnsupported: true }`, in which case the player runs only the supported groups and exposes `readonly skipped: readonly UnsupportedEffect[]`. Fail closed by default: wrong animation on stage is worse than none.
C. Tests with `bun test`. bun test runs in a JSDOM-free environment by default, and JSDOM does not implement the Web Animations API — so structure the code for testability: put the pure logic (keyframe construction, motion-path conversion, group scheduling order, prepare-hidden set computation) in exported pure functions and unit-test those directly with no DOM. Then add ONE DOM-level test using a minimal fake: a small object implementing `getElementById` and elements implementing `animate()` that record calls and return a fake Animation with a resolved `finished` promise. Assert the exact keyframes, durations, delays, and ordering. Do NOT test by asserting prose or by mocking so hard that nothing real is exercised.

TDD IS MANDATORY: write each failing test first, run `bun test` from packages/slide-runtime, confirm the failure reason, then implement.

HARD CONSTRAINTS (repo law, non-negotiable — see CONTRIBUTING.md and the existing packages):
- TypeScript strict; NO `any`, NO type assertions (`as any`/`as unknown`), NO non-null `!`, NO `@ts-ignore`, NO `enum` (use `as const` + literal unions), NO default exports.
- `readonly` on all interface/type properties; `readonly T[]` for arrays; `import type` for type-only imports.
- Zod at the boundary (the JSON), plain readonly types internally.
- Exhaustive `switch` on discriminated unions ending in `default: assertNever(x)`.
- Typed errors: an Error subclass with a machine-readable `code` field; no bare `throw new Error("string")` for domain failures; no empty catch, no catch-and-swallow.
- SECURITY BOUNDARY (enforced by repo checks): browser packages must NOT import AI provider SDKs, model runtimes, node builtins, or private contracts. This package must have ZERO runtime dependencies except zod. Keep it browser-safe.
- Every file under 250 lines.
- Verify with: `cd packages/slide-runtime && bun test` (green) and `bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (clean) and `bunx biome check src` (clean). Run these and paste the output.
- DO NOT RUN git commit/add or any git write command. The lead commits.
- DO NOT modify the root package.json, other packages, or anything under services/ or apps/.

VERIFY before reporting: bun test green, tsc clean, biome clean.
STOP WHEN: the package exists with all files above, every test passes, the three gates are clean, and you have reported the exported API surface plus pasted command output.

If a long phase is running, report `WORKING: <phase>`; report `BLOCKED: <reason>` only if truly stuck.
